title: Rava of Barnish
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: Hyman says he always discusses matters with Rav Ashi, as in [Shabbat 28a](https://www.sefaria.org/Shabbat.28a.7-8), where he said to Rav Ashi, “One can refute…” — “rather, Rava of Barnish said”; in [Rosh Hashanah 26b](https://www.sefaria.org/Rosh_Hashanah.26b.1) he said to Rav Ashi, “If I had been there I would have said to him: How did he ‘kava’ you [i.e., rob you]?” etc.; in [Bava Metzia 73b](https://www.sefaria.org/Bava_Metzia.73b.3) he said to Rav Ashi, “Let the Master see the Rabbis who eat interest”; and in [Zevachim 11a](https://www.sefaria.org/Zevachim.11a.7) he said to Rav Ashi, “But let us refute… — rather,” etc.
Hyman infers from this that he took part with Rav Ashi in arranging the Talmud.

Hyman reports that he spoke to Rava in [Nazir 31a](https://www.sefaria.org/Nazir.31a.7) and [Nazir 40a](https://www.sefaria.org/Nazir.40a.15); Hyman suggests that possibly it was written לרב״א, an abbreviation for Rav Ashi.[^3]

notes.text: Saved Davidson Rosh Hashanah 26b establishes קבע as rob in this episode. The unfamiliar word remains visible in the translated question, rather than being mistranslated fix. The always assertion, Talmud-arrangement inference and proposed Rav-Ashi abbreviation remain Hyman’s.
Hyman’s “always” and his inference concerning participation in arranging the Talmud are retained. The Rava/Rav Ashi abbreviation proposal remains his conjecture.

Both linked Nazir passages already name Rav Ashi as the addressee, as does [Seder HaDorot](https://www.girsology.com/seder-hadorot.html?entry=3090&lang=en). Hyman reports a Rava reading and proposes that the letters may abbreviate Rav Ashi. The linked dialogue is distinct from his inference about arranging the Talmud.
